title: Tutti Frutti
build: Contributor-supplied two-stage packed PRG, PAL. Release provenance unverified.

records.c: BASIC line 1 checks whether $2000 already begins with SEI ($78). If so, it starts the unpacked engine immediately with SYS 8192.
BASIC lines 10 through 50 call SYS 5376, clear and color the display, point TED at the custom character set and turn on multicolor text.
BASIC lines 60 and 70 position and print the Mastertronic Presents credit.
BASIC lines 80 through 200 print two groups of character cells for the Tutti Frutti lettering. TED uses the publisher screen glyphs at $2000 at this point.
BASIC lines 210 and 220 print the Mr Chip Software credit and set TED's screen colors.
BASIC lines 230 and 240 run one step of the logo animation per loop and poll GET. A key or 240 passes exits the wait.
BASIC line 250 calls SYS 9256 to unpack and start the resident game. A zero link after this line ends the BASIC listing.
Bytes after BASIC's zero link begin with seven-byte variable-format records for T, A$ and Z. The running BASIC program allocates its live variables from $2400.
Bit patterns following the retained BASIC records. The displayed publisher glyphs are fetched from $2000 and the resident game's glyphs from $3800. The original use of these earlier bytes is unknown.
A second set of BASIC variable-format records with the same variable names and a different saved value for T. BASIC's live variable pointer is $2400 during the publisher screen.
BASIC line 10 calls this immediate return. The packed file has already prepared the publisher screen's character set by the time this instruction runs.
Copies corresponding bytes from $2000-$23FF to $3800-$3BFF, with X as the byte index within each page.
The pair $01,$00 immediately precedes the game's music routine. The routine starts at $1780 and reads its note data at $3F00.

Advances the tune on every eighth unmuted call. The high nibble of each byte selects voice 1's pitch, with 1 holding the previous note. On the preceding call it gates the voice off for a fresh attack unless the next token holds. Holding Shift keeps the voice gated off and pauses this reader's counters.
Screen codes for the score, time, bonus, level and top-score labels. The HUD builder copies the rows to the panel on the right of the orchard.
Six cells for TIME, including its trailing blanks.
Six cells for BONUS, including its trailing blank.
Six cells for LEVEL, including its trailing blank.
Six cells for TOP above the score table.
Eight rows of five screen-code digits, ordered from 10000 down to 03000. Each row ends with a blank cell.
Default second place, stored in the panel's digit codes.
Default third place, stored in the panel's digit codes.
Default fourth place, stored in the panel's digit codes.
Default fifth place, stored in the panel's digit codes.
Default sixth place, stored in the panel's digit codes.
Default seventh place, stored in the panel's digit codes.
Default eighth place, stored in the panel's digit codes.
A zero immediately after the eighth default score row.
The score shifter indexes from one byte before the row-low table, so X selects row X minus one. Its index is already in the high-score part of the screen.
Low bytes of the first 24 row addresses in the 40-column screen at $0C00. Attribute accesses use the same low byte.
The final low-table byte is also the base for indexed reads of the previous row's high byte. An X greater than zero lands in the high table that follows.
High bytes of the first 24 row addresses at $0C00. Subtracting four gives the corresponding address in the attribute plane at $0800.
Upper-left screen glyph for each of the eight layout nibble values.
Upper-right screen glyph for each of the eight layout nibble values.
Lower-left screen glyph for each of the eight layout nibble values.
Lower-right screen glyph for each of the eight layout nibble values.
Attribute constants indexed by layout nibble. The renderer uses entries 0 and 4–7 directly; types 1–3 take their row-dependent attributes from $34D0 instead.
Rows of screen codes for the in-game title, with credit, control prompt and fruit characters interleaved with the lettering.
Twenty-four screen codes for the copyright row, including the four year digits.
Twenty-four screen codes for the Shaun Southern credit.
Twenty-four screen codes for the Acid Apples caption.
Twenty-four screen codes for PRESS FIRE TO START and its margin.
Sixteen screen codes: three blanks, FEATURING and four periods.
The upper row of the pictured strawberry and its SUPER caption.
The lower row of the pictured strawberry and its STRAWBERRY caption.
Five pairs of upper Acid Apple glyphs with one space between each pair.
Five pairs of lower Acid Apple glyphs lined up under the faces at $1950.
Toggles $B4 and subtracts one from the three decimal screen-code digits on alternate calls. At 000 it sets the death state and starts its $C0 countdown.
Counts 60 calls in $B5 before advancing the HUD's seconds. The tens digits roll over after 5 and the units after 9, up through both minute digits.
Adds the displayed three-digit bonus to the score, starting with its units. A blank is not needed because zero has its own screen code.
Enters the round-clear state, then adds to the score's thousands digit from the layout index plus one, reduced by three when it is at least four.
Adds A to the X-th displayed score digit at $0C4A. Rolls a digit above 9 back by ten and carries one left, stopping when X runs off the five-digit field.
Leaves the score adder when the updated digit is below ten.
Adds 25 points, using the tens and units of the on-screen score.
Requests the hit sound and adds 100 points to the on-screen score.
Requests the hit sound for an apple or sliding-fruit kill. Adds 250 points except in state 6, where it adds 100.
Counts down the game-over display and plays its two-voice phrase from the two sixteen-entry pitch tables. At zero it resets the stack, changes to title state and jumps to the title music reset.
Decrements the game-over timer. The middle $80 ticks play the two pitch tables, while the outer parts are silent.
On the $A0 game-over tick, puts the Game Over message in the middle of the orchard and blanks the rows above and below it.
Increments the layout counter, visible two-digit level and difficulty index. Clamps the lookup index to 15 and reads the spawn quota and enemy speed from two parallel tables.
Sets bit 7 of the current game state. If a ball is active, clears its recorded screen cell. The comparison with state 6 after setting bit 7 cannot skip that erase.
Saves the current screen row pointer and Y offset so the death path can erase the displayed ball.

Adds the enemy speed to an eight-bit accumulator and updates the five enemy slots on carry. Counts down queued spawns and then moves each active apple one coordinate unit (two display pixels). Calls the bonus tick after the enemy update.
At an enemy's tile boundary, chooses its next direction and clears its current logical tile.

Builds a four-bit mask of open neighboring cells on the 16-by-12 orchard. Suppresses a reverse when another exit exists, then samples random directions until one matches. Reverses if the remaining mask is empty.

Checks the active ball against five enemy positions and awards its hit score. Moves the ball to cooldown and removes its drawn mark on a hit. Also checks all eight moving-fruit slots against the enemies.
Decrements the ball state while it is neither zero nor active. At $20 it requests the ready sound.
Compares active moving fruit with active enemy coordinates. A hit deactivates the enemy, scores for the fruit and requests the hit effect.

With a nonzero reserve on entry, queues every slot whose direction and timer are both $FF. A countdown of 64–127 activates after 65–128 enemy updates. When more slots are free than remain in reserve, the subtraction wraps the reserve byte.
Clears the round once its reserve and all five live and pending enemy slots are empty.
Tests the player against moving fruit in slots 5 through 0 and then enemies in slots 5 through 1. A hit sets the death bit and loads a $C0 countdown.
Counts down the death pause and drives both TED voices from a pitch calculated from the countdown. At zero it takes a life and clears the death bit from the resulting state.
Decrements the death countdown. Between $9F and $61 it programs both TED voices with a pitch derived from the timer.
Decrements the displayed life digit. A remaining life goes to the restart routine, while zero selects state 7 and gives the Game Over sequence its $C0 countdown.
Selects Game Over after the life digit reaches zero and loads its countdown.
Draws a solid 2-by-2 block at the spawn point and cycles its luminance from the frame counter. A pending spawn with fewer than 50 steps remaining changes the hue.
Adds $B13579 with carry to the 24-bit state at $89-$8B. Returns the updated high byte in A for turn and spawn choices.
Configures TED's custom text screen and color registers. Installs the handler at $20A0 in the KERNAL IRQ vector, clears the board and HUD, and falls into the title setup.
Resets the tune counters, its wrap counter and the state selector before falling through to the idle loop.
Foreground loop reads TED's border register and jumps back. The raster interrupt advances the title, play, death and end-of-game states.

Checks and acknowledges TED's raster flag, programs line 200 for the next interrupt and increments the frame counter. Dispatches by the game state in $E2 and jumps to the KERNAL register-pop return at $FCC3.
Dispatches states with bit 7 set to the death sequence, then returns through the KERNAL.

Compares the five on-screen score digits against the next higher row of the table. Moves overtaken entries down and writes the current score in its new slot. Colors that slot from an eight-entry sequence indexed by the frame counter.
Uses the current rank to locate the row above it and compares the five digits from most to least significant. After any promotion it shifts the intervening scores down.

Advances the two-voice theme, showing six layouts on successive 32-note boundaries of alternate passes. Draws the title on the other pass and checks port 1 for fire. Fire starts the round transition and resets score-panel and difficulty state.
Ticks the interlude until its delay reaches zero, then restores the saved 8-by-3 patch of screen codes and attributes and advances the state to active play.
Copies an 8-by-3 patch of the orchard and its attributes into page four. Replaces it with the small round message using the screen codes at $3EEC.
Orders the play update from music and control through fruit, enemies, drawing, clear and death tests. Updates the time display and compares the live score with the high-score table at the end.
Decrements the interlude delay. Its upper range selects a pair of pitches from $3EC8 and $3ED4, and reaching $80 starts the round setup.
At tile alignment, looks one cell ahead of moving fruit slot 7. A nonempty cell stops the slide and puts the fruit back onto the board at its current position.
Redraws a settled Bad Apple with the four glyphs starting at $40, then plays the low form of the short tone.
Redraws a settled cherry with the four glyphs starting at $68, then plays the low form of the short tone.
Counts down the cherry crush. Changes the four character cells to the next crush frame on selected ticks, then clears the logical tile and the displayed cells when the count expires.
Writes one attribute to the four cells at the current screen pointer. Uses the block-mode color in state 6 and the normal tunnel color otherwise, then switches the pointer back to screen codes.
Reads the logical tile at X,Y. Leaves an apple alone and scores and sounds a cherry before clearing its tile. Other values fall through to the clear.
Consumes a pending one-tick sound hold before advancing the effect generator.
Writes $71 to the attribute at the ball's new cell. Once the ball has left the player's logical tile, returning to that tile clears its attribute and active state.
If a duration remains, adds the pitch increment to the pitch accumulator and sends it to TED voice 2, then decrements the duration. At zero gates voice 2 off while preserving the other control bits.
Clears a logical tile with the value in A and seeds a descending pitch for voice 2.
Runs the moving-fruit hook and zeros the effect duration.
Programs voice 2 with low byte $F0 and high bits 3, enables it and gives it a one-tick hold. The entry at $25F8 uses high bits 0 instead.
Sets voice 2's high bits to 0 and branches into the common one-tick tone at $25E5.
Converts the direction bit mask in A to one direction index. Priority is down, up, right, left. Returns $FF if no direction bit is set.
Stores the decoded direction in actor slot 0. Copies the push flag in $ED into the direction's high bit when that flag is set.
Intersects joystick direction with the legal neighbor mask in $E8. If no requested direction survives, falls back to continuing the previous direction where it remains legal.

On fire, with the ball state at zero, starts a diagonal shot using the current direction's velocity pair. Snaps the ball to the middle horizontally and top vertically of the player's tile. State 6 bypasses the launcher.

Erases the old ball, tests its horizontal and vertical destinations against the logical tile map, and reflects velocity on the blocked axes. A blocked diagonal flips both. Advances position and selects a quarter-cell glyph from the low coordinate bits.
Clears the four character pages and fills their attribute pages. Draws the panel labels, default scores, border and lives icon from the screen-code records and the four strawberry cells.
Zeros the displayed score, elapsed time, bonus and level. Sets the lives digit to 5 and places the two timer separators.
Selects a 96-byte layout at $3500 + 96*X. Decodes its high and low nibbles left to right into 16 columns and 12 rows, draws each metatile, then copies the packed layout to the mutable map at $0600.
Takes X as the tile value and D8:D9 plus Y as the first screen cell. Copies four glyph indices from the parallel tables and asks the palette selector for the two attribute rows.
Copies ten rows of screen codes from $18A8-$196F to their fixed positions. Colors the text and the strawberry and Acid Apple cells.

Divides the calling tick by eight and plays a packed pair of pitch indexes from the 192-byte score. A high nibble of 1 ties voice 1 across the previous tick's gate boundary. The low nibble picks voice 2's pitch.
Tests the low three bits of the player’s two position coordinates. Runs tile-entry logic only when both are aligned to an 8-unit tile boundary (16 display pixels).
In state 2, scans both nibbles of every map byte for cherry value 2 and takes the special clear once none remains. State 4 also requires exactly six grounded apple tiles in the last row.
Loads $E0 into the interlude timer and moves the selector from active play to the next odd state, wrapping state 7 to 1. Adds the remaining bonus to the score.
Takes the special clear path, which adds a layout-dependent thousands bonus as well as the displayed bonus.
Combines the four corner nibbles and compares the common bits with 5, the Bad Apple block code. The match takes the special clear path.

Decrements the per-fruit delay indexed by X. While the delay remains, discards its own return address and returns to the play tick. On expiry converts the fruit's coordinates to a tile, clears it and starts the movement effect.

When fire is held at a tile boundary, checks the tile ahead and the tile beyond it. Starts a slide for either block type if the next tile is empty. A cherry with a blocked path starts its crush animation and earns 25 points.
A type-5 block with open space ahead selects the Bad Apple’s graphics and branches to the common slide setup at $2D34.
A type-4 block with an occupied cell beyond it starts a 32-tick crush, records its screen pointer, and scores for the cherry.
Exits the push dispatcher for a blocked apple or an unsupported tile type.
Returns the constant attribute for space and apple or cherry blocks. Uses a row palette for the other tiles, offset by twelve rows in round transition state 3.

Between tile boundaries allows only the current axis and filters the joystick through it. At a tile boundary checks all four neighbors and records a blocked direction with bit 7 set for the push logic.

At a tile boundary, reads the controller and tests the four neighboring tiles. Stores a legal direction when one is requested. With a blocked direction, keeps the intended facing with bit 7 set so a fire press can push the obstacle.
On even frame counts, moves the player one position unit (two display pixels) in its direction if the direction’s high bit is clear.
Makes a joystick-style mask from the adjacent cells. Allows space, soil and normal cherries and leaves apples and sliding blocks out.
Sets carry if X is at least 16 or Y at least 12. Unsigned comparisons also reject coordinates that have wrapped below zero.
Clears or collects the tile under the player. If the player is between cells and moving, also visits the other tile overlapped along the direction axis.
Sets the high bit of the player direction byte while preserving the direction index.
Returns map nibble (X,Y) in A. Even columns use the high nibble of $0600 + 8*Y + floor(X/2). An out-of-range coordinate returns $0F.
Four NOPs lie between the out-of-bounds return and the branch target for valid coordinates.
Computes the packed row offset and extracts the high nibble for an even column or the low nibble for an odd one.
Writes A into the nibble at map coordinate X,Y while preserving its neighbor in the same byte. The caller supplies a valid coordinate.
Two $79 bytes between the tile helpers and the draw queue. The actor draw queue loads the same color as an immediate value at $3079.

Converts player and enemy positions into screen pointers. Uses the movement axis and the half-cell phase to select a drawing record. Appends the record's screen addresses, glyphs and attributes to the draw buffer.
Gets a base strawberry glyph from the drawing table. For any nonzero actor slot, adds $1E to select the Acid Apple version.
Clears the screen codes at the previous draw buffer's addresses. Sets the queue count to $FF when done.
Writes each queued glyph and attribute at the stored screen pointer, from the last record back to the first.

Reads TED with the port 1 select bit low and merges four keys from the keyboard matrix into the active-low direction bits. Returns the four directions active high and the fire signal active low in bit 7 of $F6.

Advances the stage and difficulty, wraps the layout index after five, draws layout index plus one and saves the area hidden by the interlude. Loads sixteen fruit-coordinate bytes before falling through to the player and enemy reset.

Clears motion and deactivates the fruit and enemy slots, puts the player at (56,8), resets effects and the enemy accumulator, and initializes the bonus to 599, 799 or 999 according to the round's state.
Walks eight moving-fruit slots. Uses direction and subcell phase to choose a draw record and appends its addresses and glyphs to the queue, then converts the queue's next index into its last index.
Gets the glyph from the moving-fruit table. Slot 7 uses the offset in $64 to choose between the sliding Bad Apple and cherry graphics.
Stores attribute $5A for state 6 and $08 for the other rounds in the queued cell.

Skips gravity in the block round. For each of the six Bad Apple slots it tests the tile beneath. Empty space starts the fall and seeds the delay on entry to falling state. A blocked tile ends an active fall.
Converts the stopped apple's position to a tile, writes the apple code there and redraws the four screen cells.
Gives a newly falling apple a delay of $20. An apple already marked as falling keeps its current timer.

Visits the eight active fruit slots from 7 down to 0. A zero delay adds its two velocity bytes to position. A nonzero delay calls the delay routine, which returns directly to the play tick while the wait remains.
Sets the first glyph to $40 for a stationary Bad Apple and enters the shared 2-by-2 draw.
Sets the first glyph to $68 for a stationary cherry block and enters the shared 2-by-2 draw.
Converts the tile in $E9,$EA to its screen address and writes four consecutive glyphs starting at X. Leaves the address in $D8:$D9 for the attribute routine.
Eight inclusive start indexes into the moving-fruit glyph and offset tables, selected by axis and subcell phase.
Eight exclusive end indexes paired with the starts at $3400.
44 glyph codes for the pixel phases of moving fruit. Slot 7 adds $64's offset to select its Bad Apple or cherry art.
44 relative screen offsets paired with the moving-fruit glyphs. Values 40 and above select cells one or two rows below the anchor.
Delay bytes for the actor reset. Slots 1 through 5 start with $20,$30,$40,$50,$60, while indices 6 and 7 start at zero.
Maps a single direction bit to the direction index, used by the enemy turn selector after sampling a legal exit.
Sixteen low pitch bytes for the first TED voice during Game Over. The countdown reads them in descending index order.
Sixteen low pitch bytes for TED's second voice during Game Over.
Sixteen screen-code bytes for the Game Over line, including the exclamation marks.
Sixteen entries for difficulty indexes 0–15. The reserve values of 0–8 supplement the five enemy slots scheduled at round setup.
Per-difficulty increment for the enemy movement accumulator. Carry in $1C00 triggers an enemy update.
Twelve normal row attributes followed by twelve alternate row attributes. State 3 selects the second set for the matching layout.
Eight attributes for the current score's row in the high-score table, indexed by the low three frame bits.
Packed 16-by-12 tile map with a clear center and alternating fruit around the edges. The title routine prints over its center.
Packed first orchard with 32 cherries, six Bad Apples and a pre-cut route to the spawn. Its active state is 2.
Packed second orchard with six cherries, six Bad Apples and a solid top edge. Its active state is 4.
Packed first block orchard with 64 cherry blocks and four Bad Apple blocks. Its active state is 6.
Packed second cherry orchard with 40 cherries and six Bad Apples. Reuses active state 2.
Packed alternate grounded-apple orchard with six cherries and six Bad Apples. Reuses active state 4.
Packed alternate block orchard with 72 cherry blocks and four Bad Apple blocks. Reuses active state 6.
Eight X bytes followed by eight Y bytes in two-display-pixel units. Six positions match the type-3 apple tiles in the first orchard and $FF marks unused positions.
Six fallable apple positions for layout two, in parallel X and Y arrays with two unused slots.
Empty falling-fruit positions for the first block round. Its apples stay in the tile map until pushed.
Six fallable apple positions for the second cherry orchard.
Six fallable apple positions for the second grounded-apple orchard.
Empty falling-fruit positions for the second block round.
TED reads eight bytes per character. This first group covers blank, the letters, the solid cell and digits zero through three. Later groups at $3900-$3E7F provide the rest of the artwork.
Patterns $20-$3F complete the numeric alphabet and include the four ball quadrants and the four groups of breaking-fruit cells.
Patterns $40-$5F hold the aligned Bad Apple and most of its shifted drawing pieces.
Patterns $60-$7F finish the Bad Apple's shifted pieces and begin the corresponding cherry shapes.
Patterns $80-$9F finish the shifted cherries and begin the strawberry's position-dependent cells.
Patterns $A0-$BF finish the strawberry and start the Acid Apple shapes. The enemy draw codes use the same geometry with a glyph bias of $1E.
Patterns $C0-$CB complete the Acid Apple shapes. $CC-$CF are the four soil cells. The next byte begins drawing tables.
Six inclusive start offsets into the actor drawing records. The two axes and horizontal facings choose a pair of subcell phases.
Six exclusive end offsets paired with the starts at $3E80.
30 glyph codes for the strawberry's draw records. The Acid Apple uses the same positions with $1E added to each glyph.
30 relative screen offsets for the strawberry and enemy shapes.
Twelve low pitch bytes for the second TED voice during a clear interlude.
Twelve low pitch bytes for the first TED voice during a clear interlude.
Four zeros separate the twelve voice 1 pitch bytes from the ball's horizontal speeds.
Horizontal speed of -2 or +2 for each of the four player directions when a ball is fired.
Vertical speed of -2 or +2 for each of the four player directions when a ball is fired.
Eight character codes copied into the middle row of the temporary round-start panel, spelling READY! with a blank on either side.
Direction bits for left, right, up and down. Also used to mask out an enemy's reverse direction.
Signed horizontal step for left, right, up and down. Callers add it either to a position in two-display-pixel units or to a tile column.
Signed vertical step for left, right, up and down. Callers add it either to a position in two-display-pixel units or to a tile row.
192 paired note tokens shared by the title and gameplay theme. The high nibble is voice 1, with 1 holding its note. The title also reads the low nibble for voice 2.
Voice 1's low pitch byte by note nibble.
Voice 1's high pitch bits by note nibble, written to $FF12.
Voice 2's low pitch byte by note nibble.
Unused low-pitch table tail. The shared score's voice 2 nibbles range from 2 to 9.
Voice 2's high pitch bits by note nibble, written to $FF10.
Unused high-pitch table tail. The final two values are present in the hand-over image, beyond the score's largest voice 2 nibble, 9.
